title: Biggest Buyers
story: Rank customers by how many units they really received: delivered orders only.
goal: Show each customer's name and total delivered quantity as total_qty, biggest first.
starter:
SELECT c.name, SUM(o.qty) AS total_qty
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
;

tests.label: Hidden check on other data
Hidden check on other data

hints: Join, filter, then GROUP BY the customer name and SUM the quantity.
Sort with ORDER BY total_qty DESC.
SELECT c.name, SUM(o.qty) AS total_qty FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY total_qty DESC;
socratic: Compare the rows you got with the rows expected. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what does your query do?
solution: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.qty) AS total_qty FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY total_qty DESC;
alt: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.qty) AS total_qty FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY 2 DESC;
